name: Web Cache Poisoning (Unkeyed Input)
description: Poisons a shared web cache by getting a harmful response stored against a normal cache key. The attack targets unkeyed inputs - request components the cache ignores for keying but the origin reflects into the response - most commonly X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Host, and other headers, plus unkeyed query params and fat GET bodies. Distinct from cache deception (which serves one user's private content to another). Uses Param Miner to discover unkeyed inputs.
source: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - Web cache poisoning
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  A cache stores a response under a key (usually method + host + path + some query). Inputs NOT in the key are 'unkeyed'. If the origin reflects an unkeyed input into the response (e.g. builds an absolute URL from X-Forwarded-Host), you can poison the cached copy served to everyone hitting that key.

=== METHOD ===
  1. Find an unkeyed input that is reflected (Param Miner > 'Guess headers' / 'Guess params').
  2. Confirm the response is cached (Age / X-Cache: hit / Cache-Control headers; identical response on repeat).
  3. Inject a payload via the unkeyed input that reflects into the cached response.
  4. Re-request the clean URL - the poisoned response is served from cache.

=== CLASSIC UNKEYED HEADERS ===
  X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Forwarded-Scheme, X-Forwarded-Server, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL, Forwarded.

=== PAYLOAD CLASSES ===
  - Reflected XSS into a cached page (steal many users' sessions).
  - Cached redirect to attacker.com via X-Forwarded-Host in a Location/script src.
  - Import malicious script by poisoning a reflected host in a <script src> base.
  - DoS: poison with an oversized/invalid header to cache an error.

=== CACHE-KEY TRICKS ===
  - Cache-key normalization: path?utm=... may be unkeyed; find a param the origin uses but the cache ignores.
  - 'Fat GET': a GET with a body that the origin parses but the cache does not key on.

=== TOOLING ===
  - Burp extension 'Param Miner' (Guess headers, Guess GET params, Bulk scan).
  - Watch X-Cache, Age, CF-Cache-Status, Cache-Control, Vary in responses.

examples.label: Poison with X-Forwarded-Host to import attacker script
Confirm caching via the Age / X-Cache headers
Param Miner bulk header guess
examples.command: Burp > target > Extensions > Param Miner > 'Guess headers'

recommended.note: Sibling cache class - deception serves private content rather than poisoning a shared key.
Host-header reflection is a primary unkeyed input for poisoning.
Reflected XSS delivered via a poisoned cache magnifies impact across all users.

defense.why_it_works: The cache keys on a subset of the request; any input the origin reflects but the cache omits from the key (unkeyed) lets an attacker store a harmful response that is then served to every user requesting the normal URL.
defense.prerequisites: A caching layer (CDN/reverse proxy) in front of an origin that reflects an unkeyed input into cacheable responses, and a cacheable resource.
defense.impact: Mass delivery of reflected XSS, malicious script imports, forced redirects, or denial of service to every user served the poisoned cache entry - a stored, wide-blast-radius attack.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1659] Requests carrying X-Forwarded-Host/X-Host/X-Forwarded-Scheme or other off-host header values, cache responses whose reflected host differs from the real host, and sudden changes in a cached resource's content hash.
defense.artifacts: CDN/reverse-proxy access logs showing anomalous forwarding headers, cache hit/miss and Age headers, and origin logs correlating reflected header values in response bodies.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web
| rex field=_raw "X-Forwarded-Host:\s*(?<xfh>[^\r\n]+)"
| where isnotnull(xfh) AND xfh!="<target>"
| stats count by clientip, xfh, uri_path
defense.sentinel_kql:
AZFWApplicationRule
| where RequestHeaders has "X-Forwarded-Host"
| extend xfh = extract(@"X-Forwarded-Host:\s*([^\r\n;]+)", 1, RequestHeaders)
| where isnotempty(xfh) and xfh != "<target>"
| summarize count() by SourceIp, xfh
defense.prevention: Add every input the origin reflects to the cache key (or stop reflecting it). Strip untrusted X-Forwarded-* / Forwarded headers at the edge. Set explicit Vary headers, disable caching of responses that reflect request data, and never build absolute URLs or script sources from client-supplied host headers.

detections.name: Off-host X-Forwarded-Host header reaching a cacheable path
detections.logic:
index=web sourcetype=nginx
| rex field=_raw "X-Forwarded-Host:\s*(?<xfh>[^\r\n]+)"
| where isnotnull(xfh) AND NOT match(xfh, "^<target>$") AND like(status, "2%")
| stats count by clientip, xfh, uri_path
detections.false_positives: Legitimate multi-tier proxies that set X-Forwarded-Host to known internal hosts.
detections.tuning: Allow-list expected forwarding hosts set by your own edge; alert only on externally supplied values.
